ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The image of the force F acting on an object changing with displacement x is shown in the figure. How much work does force F do on the object in this process?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the graph: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled F/N, and the horizontal axis is labeled x/m. The graph line shows that from x=0 to x=3 m, force F remains at 2 N; from x=3 m to x=5 m, the graph line is a downward-sloping straight line, linearly decreasing from F=2 N to F=-2 N, and intersects the x-axis at x=4 m. The figure also has vertical dashed lines at x=3 and x=5 and a horizontal dashed line at F=-2 N as reading aids. Then reason: When force changes with displacement, the work done by the force is equal to the signed area enclosed by the F-x graph and the x-axis. The part from 0 to 3 m is a rectangle, and the work W1=2×3=6 J. The part from 3 to 5 m can be regarded as a trapezoid with linear change, and the signed area W2=[2+(-2)]/2×(5-3)=0 J; it can also be understood as the area 1 J of the triangle above from 3 to 4 m and the area -1 J of the triangle below from 4 to 5 m canceling each other. Therefore the total work W=W1+W2=6+0=6 J.
